T0.scene_summary: A narrow galley kitchen with a stove on the left, a long counter and cabinets on the right, and a doorway and potted plant at the far end.
T0.overall_evidence: The main kitchen arrangement and distinctive colored stove controls are recognizable. However, the reconstruction changes the framing and scale of the foreground stove, simplifies the cabinetry and finishes, and loses much of the reference's contrast, texture and directional light.

main_defects.description: The view is more centered and level, with a smaller, heavily cropped stove at the lower left, rather than the large stove dominating the left foreground. The doorway is also more central and the counter recedes differently.
main_defects.evidence: The reference stove spans roughly the left 43% of the image and extends almost to the bottom; the reconstruction stove occupies roughly the left third and is clipped at the bottom and left edges. The doorway shifts from around the center to just left of center.
main_defects.uncertainty: Differences in object size and placement may contribute alongside camera framing.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is much paler and smoother, losing the reference's prominent wood-grain floor, dark stove surfaces, textured teal counter edge and strongly contrasting cabinet colors.
main_defects.evidence: The reference floor has visible warm wood grain and the stove front is nearly black-green; the reconstructed floor is almost white with simple seams and the stove is a lighter, flat teal.
main_defects.uncertainty: The pale appearance may partly result from lighting or exposure rather than material settings alone.

main_defects.description: The strong directional lighting and contrast in the reference are largely absent, including the bright angled patch on the floor and the dark doorway interior.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a sharply defined bright floor stripe and a near-black lower doorway, while the reconstruction is evenly washed in light with a gray doorway strip.
main_defects.uncertainty: The doorway difference could also reflect a different door or background surface.

main_defects.description: The visible cabinet and drawer layout is simplified and differs in the number, scale and arrangement of fronts, particularly along the right base unit.
main_defects.evidence: The reference shows large white doors and several contrasting dark and wood-toned fronts, including a large dark foreground panel; the reconstruction shows a repeated sequence of smaller pastel and gray drawers.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some differences in apparent panel size and visibility may be due to the changed viewpoint and cropping.

main_defects.description: The stove's control panel is reduced to a plain rectangular slab with two knobs, omitting the visible central clock and the reference's angled metallic panel appearance.
main_defects.evidence: The reference panel visibly reads 12:01 between the purple knobs, while no display is visible on the reconstruction panel.
main_defects.uncertainty: The camera angle and small rendered size may obscure finer markings.

strengths: The galley layout places the stove on the left and long cabinetry on the right.
A rear doorway and a small potted plant are present in corresponding general positions.
The stove has a light cooktop with circular burners and two purple control knobs, and the right counter has a pale surface with upper cabinets above it.
T0.uncertainty: Assessment is based only on the two visible images. Camera and exposure differences can account for some apparent size, color and layout discrepancies; hidden geometry cannot be assessed. The score is an initial automated judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric.

T1.scene_summary: A narrow bright galley kitchen with a stove on the left, cabinets and a countertop on the right, and a potted plant beside a rear doorway.
T1.overall_evidence: The reconstruction preserves the main galley arrangement and recognizable appliances, cabinetry, plant and doorway. Its framing changes the relative size and placement of major elements, while the dark doorway, strongly contrasting appliance and cabinet materials, floor texture, and directional sunlight of the reference are substantially softened or missing.

main_defects.description: The view is framed more centrally and farther toward the rear: the stove is cropped at the left and bottom, the right-hand counter begins farther back in the image, and the doorway and plant appear nearer the center. In the reference the stove occupies a larger, fully visible foreground mass and the right counter fills more of the foreground.
main_defects.evidence: The reference stove body reaches the floor and is visible almost entirely; the reconstruction stove is cut off by both image edges. The rear doorway shifts from around the middle of the reference to left of center in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent differences in object size and position could arise from geometry rather than camera framing alone.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction has a much paler, flatter surface palette. The reference has a distinct wood-grain floor, dark textured stove body, pronounced dark and colored cabinet fronts, and a turquoise rear counter, while corresponding reconstructed surfaces are largely smooth and washed out.
main_defects.evidence: Wood grain and strong dark/light contrasts are clearly visible in the reference; the reconstructed floor shows pale plain planks and the cabinetry and stove are much lighter.
main_defects.uncertainty: Lighting and exposure may account for part of the color and contrast difference.

main_defects.description: The rear opening reads differently: the reference shows a dark opening and a narrow angled dark door edge, whereas the reconstruction is largely blocked by a broad white panel with only a narrow gray opening visible on its left.
main_defects.evidence: A wide black-to-gray vertical area is visible behind the reference doorway, compared with a narrow gray strip and a large white face in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The change could partly reflect a different viewing angle or lighting rather than a different door model.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction lacks the reference's strong directional illumination and shadows, notably the bright diagonal patch across the floor and the dark gradient at the doorway; the room instead appears evenly and diffusely lit.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a sharply bounded diagonal light patch on the floor and a deep dark doorway, neither of which appears comparably in the reconstruction.
main_defects.uncertainty: The dark opening also depends on doorway geometry and background, not lighting alone.

main_defects.description: The stove control panel is simplified: its reference face has an angled profile, two detailed knobs and a central digital readout, while the reconstruction has a plain rectangular face without the readout. The burner arrangement also appears different, with five visible disks rather than six.
main_defects.evidence: The reference clearly shows a central 12:01 display and six circular cooktop elements; the reconstruction shows no display and five visible elements.
main_defects.uncertainty: The image crop may hide part of the reconstructed cooktop, so the visible burner count does not establish its full geometry.

strengths: The overall narrow galley layout is recognizable, with the stove on the left and a long counter and drawers on the right.
The rear doorway, nearby potted plant, upper cabinets, and rear left counter are all represented in approximately corresponding relationships.
The stove retains a teal body, pale cooktop, circular burners, two purple controls and a purple oven handle.
The right counter retains a light marble-like surface and a mixture of differently colored drawer fronts.
T1.uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual estimate, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. Different camera framing, exposure and image resolution complicate separating geometry from appearance; only visible image content is assessed.
